label: D-86888e

defects.summary: Gauged sends AgyQuotaGauge.SpentWithoutReset to QuotaReset.FromText whatever `spent` is, so an undecided agy refusal (Spent == null) gets parked on stated/guess, although D10 and D5 list 'no reset_time' as cannot-check, which parks nothing for an undecided refusal.

IsActive also skips any bucket whose window is not exactly 'weekly' or '5h', so a new window name turns a spent group into GroupMissing; D6 does not have this rule and the deviations list does not record it.
'Does not park' is encoded as a fourth source string "none" with DateTimeOffset.MinValue, a sentinel inside the parking record instead of a separate case, and callers must remember to check Parks.

The spend limit is detected by matching WhyItFailed's composed text (the phrase plus EndsWith "(HTTP 429)") instead of reading api_error_status from the envelope, which ties the structured verdict to a display format.

Kimi uses the default ReadResetAsync, which runs CooldownParser.StatedReset on its reason, so a Kimi line with a parseable clause would be parked as 'stated', against the Kimi plan's D3 (its clause is never parsed) that D5 says still holds.

summary: A complete and faithful build: all 43 scenarios exist under their exact names and pass, the build, both test suites and format are green, and the structured verdict, the agy readers, the locked fail-open cooldown file with its refusal notice, the per-key aggregation, the roster exclusion, the providers member and the card all match the decisions. The plan's own contradictions (S25's past date, S34 against S41, S3's sample) are recorded truthfully as deviations, and an extra end-to-end test covers the engine wiring; what remains is a few small edge cases and design choices, chiefly an undecided agy refusal parked when the gauge names no reset.
